claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2: s8 and ledger now read "a mesh pays off only when it buys something the team needs and lacks: a gap a requirement asks to fill, or work that would otherwise be rebuilt in every codebase". Matches ADR l.51-53 (gaps no requirement asks to fill) and l.68-69 (per-codebase mTLS, retry, per-call metrics becoming costlier than a mesh). Recorded as opinion.

Round 2: s5 now attributes it: "The ADR's reasoning is that, once many services come in many languages, building mTLS, retries and per-call metrics into every codebase can cost more than a mesh." ADR l.68-69: "mỗi codebase tự làm mutual TLS, retry và số đo theo lời gọi trở nên đắt hơn một mesh". Hedged 'can', attributed; no general industry claim left.

Rows match ADR l.34-47 (A no mesh; B mTLS between all services, proxy per Pod, controllers, blast radius), l.36-38 (C: api only, cert-manager), l.74-76 (C: renewal, failure point on main way in), and claim 11 (server-only TLS: caller not authenticated).

ADR l.55-56, 66-67 (C first if only encryption), l.68-69 (teams or languages), l.70 (calls between clusters); threat-model l.72 accepts P5 on "một cluster". issues.text: Carried from round 1. The third misconception names per-call metrics, but the correction only shows a timeout, a circuit breaker and traces. I am left not knowing whether Đơn Hàng has per-call metrics without a mesh.
issues.quote: Without a mesh, services have no retries, timeouts or per-call metrics.
issues.fix: Add one clause saying where per-call measurements come from today, or drop 'per-call metrics' from the misconception.

issues.text: New in the reworded misconception 2: 'the mutual TLS lab' is not in the prerequisite summaries; the situation speaks of 'the sidecar lab', where two Caddy proxies also did mTLS with no mesh. I cannot tell whether these are the same lab or a different one. Quiz q4 explanation d repeats it.
issues.quote: the mutual TLS lab did mTLS in Caddy with no mesh
issues.fix: Either write 'the sidecar lab's two Caddy proxies did mTLS with no mesh', or add [[k8s.l4.mutual-tls]] to 'Before you start' so the reader knows which lab is meant.

issues.text: The meaning of 'blast radius' I know is 'everything an attacker can reach with what one compromised part holds'. Here (and in quiz q2) it means how many calls one wrong setting or failed upgrade can break. I can follow from the sentence before it, but I had to stop and reconcile the two meanings.
issues.quote: Its blast radius is every call inside the cluster.
issues.fix: Add a few words: 'Its blast radius, here what one mistake can break rather than what an attacker can reach, is every call inside the cluster.'

issues.text: q7 (reworded): option a is clearly the longest, the only one with a two-part answer, and echoes section 8 ('builds such work into a service's own code'). I can pick it from length and wording alone.
issues.quote: Such work lives in a service's own code: Payments wraps its outside payment gateway calls, while the api has none written
issues.fix: Shorten option a, e.g. 'Payments has them in its own code; nobody wrote them for the api', or lengthen one distractor to similar size.
